The Section on "Dependent" and so forth (Paṭicca-ādi-vāra) 2.8.6.1–7.1–4.
Positive Conditions and so forth (Paccayānuloma-ādi)
Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the hindrances but is subject to the hindrances,
there arises a state dissociated from the hindrances but subject to the hindrances by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate dissociated from the hindrances but subject to the hindrances,
there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [abbreviated].
(Just as the mundane dyads in the *Cūḷantaraduka* should be treated, so it should be done here without any difference.
The dyad of those dissociated from the hindrances and those subject to the hindrances is finished.
The group on the hindrances (*nīvaraṇagocchaka*) is finished.
